summary: fix(bonusly): reject recipient mentions that won't resolve, via live lookup
reason: Mention syntax is space-free; a syntactic space check alone cannot distinguish a valid single-token mention (e.g. '@jane.doe') from a two-word display name typed as if it were one mention (e.g. '@Jane Doe', this PR's original motivating case) -- both are syntactically 'a token, then a space, then more text'. Iterated through three review rounds on PR #1899: (1) initial whitespace-after-@ check, correct but only caught a literally-empty mention; (2) fixed a stdin bypass of that same narrow check (Greptile P1); (3) a human reviewer correctly flagged that neither version caught the original '@Jane Doe'-shaped case, and a capitalization heuristic considered at that point was rejected as unsafe (it would false-positive on this CLI's own documented example, '+50 @jane.doe Great work...', since 'jane.doe' bare-lowercase + 'Great' capitalized is structurally identical to the bad case once you also consider a single-word capitalized username). Replaced the heuristic with a live resolution check against GET /users/autocomplete (the endpoint F1 fixed in this same PR) via a new shared resolveMentionCandidate() helper: every extracted @token is checked against the real user directory (username, full email, or email local-part, case-insensitive) before the mutating POST /bonuses ever fires.
validated_outcome: Live-verified end-to-end, not dry-run: `recognition create --reason "+15 @Jane Doe test #teamwork"` and the equivalent --stdin payload are both rejected before any POST fires, with live 'did you mean' suggestions pulled from the real directory (e.g. other actual Jane-prefixed users) rather than Bonusly's opaque 'Reason is incomplete' 400. give's --to with a bare unresolvable single token (no embedded space, so the old whitespace check missed it) is now also rejected client-side. A genuinely valid mention (own account's email) passes the check and reaches the real API, which then fails for an unrelated, expected reason (self-recognition), confirming no false-positive block. Under --dry-run the check is honestly reported as skipped (dry-run intercepts ALL client requests including this read, per client.Client.dryRun -- there is no way to validate resolution without a real round trip) rather than silently claiming a pass; the real submission remains the enforcement point either way.
